theme: A firm reply to Makkah’s idol-worship: calling angels Allah’s daughters, blindly following forefathers, and judging a messenger by his wealth. Worldly glitter means nothing to Allah; He alone is God and has no child.
story: Revealed in Makkah, apparently in the same period as Al-Muʾmin and Ash-Shūrā. The Quraysh were meeting day and night to plan how to get rid of the Prophet ﷺ, and an attempt had already been made on his life (79–80).

They admitted that Allah created the heavens and the earth, yet worshipped angels they called His daughters. Pressed for proof, they blamed Allah’s will and their forefathers’ ways. They also scorned the Prophet ﷺ for not being rich: why not a great man from Makkah or Ṭāʾif?

The surah answers each claim. Ibrāhīm, the ancestor they were proudest of, broke from his father’s religion. Pharaoh also sneered at Mūsā for having no gold. ʿĪsā was only a servant. Wealth is worthless to Allah, and the Prophet ﷺ is told to turn away and say “Peace.”

sections.title: The Qur’an won’t be withheld; earth, rain and mounts point to Allah
sections.meaning: By the clear Book: Allah made it an Arabic Qur’an to be understood, and it is exalted with Him. He won’t stop sending it because they go too far. Stronger mockers were destroyed. They admit Allah created all, and His gifts of earth, rain and mounts call for thanks.
points: By the clear Book: an Arabic Qur’an, exalted in the Mother of the Book
Will We stop the Reminder because you go too far?
Every prophet was mocked; stronger nations were destroyed
Ask who created the heavens and earth: they say Allah
The earth a bed, roads, measured rain, pairs, ships and cattle
Remember His favour when riding; say the traveller’s duʿāʾ
sections.matters: It sets up the whole surah: the Qur’an is from Allah, history has already warned the mockers, and even they admit Allah is the Creator. Everything after this shows how their idol-worship contradicts that admission.
sections.story: No specific incident. It consoles the Prophet ﷺ over his people’s mockery: every prophet before him was mocked too, and Allah kept sending the Reminder.
explained: Allah swears by the Qur’an itself: clear in words and meaning, in Arabic so its first hearers could understand. In umm al-kitāb, the Preserved Tablet, it is high and full of wisdom. Should He stop sending it because they turn away? No: out of mercy He kept calling them.

Every earlier prophet was mocked, and nations far stronger were destroyed. Ask them who created the heavens and earth and they say Allah. He made the earth a bed, sends rain in measure to revive dead land, just as you will be brought out, and gave you ships and animals to ride.
teaches: The Qur’an is honoured with Allah, so honour it.
Allah’s mercy keeps calling people back, even the heedless.
Rain reviving dead land is a picture of resurrection.
When you ride, remember who made it possible, and your final return.
sections.hook: Three “He who” lines in a row: made the earth a bed (10), sent down rain (11), created the pairs (12). Ayah 9’s question, “Who created…?”, comes back at 87.

sections.title: They call angels Allah’s daughters and blindly follow their forefathers’ religion
sections.meaning: Though they admit Allah is the Creator, they make some of His servants a “part” of Him: the angels as His daughters, when they hate having daughters themselves. Their proof? Allah’s will and their forefathers. Every warner heard the same excuse from the rich, and those nations were punished.
points: They made His servants His “part”: daughters for Him, sons for them
A daughter darkens their face, yet they assign daughters to Allah
Angels called female: did they witness it? It will be recorded
“If Allah willed, we wouldn’t worship them”: pure guessing
No earlier book, only “we found our fathers on a religion”
Every warner heard it from the rich; they were punished
sections.matters: It exposes the idolaters’ two main defences, “Allah willed it” and “our fathers did it”, and shows neither is knowledge. Blind following of ancestors is the excuse every nation used against its prophet.
sections.story: The idolaters called the angels Allah’s daughters. Reportedly, when the Prophet ﷺ asked how they knew, they said they heard it from their fathers, who never lied. Ayah 22 is reportedly about Quraysh leaders such as al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah and Abū Jahl.
explained: They admit Allah created everything, then give Him a juzʾ, a “part”, by calling the angels His daughters. Yet when told a daughter is born to them, their faces darken. In their eyes a girl is raised in jewellery and can’t argue her case. How can they assign to Allah what they look down on?

Did they watch the angels being created? Their claim is written down and they will be questioned. “If Allah willed, we wouldn’t worship them” is guesswork. They have no book either, just “we found our fathers on this.” The rich of every nation said the same, even to better guidance, and were punished.
teaches: Don’t attribute to Allah what you would hate for yourself.
“Allah willed it” is no excuse for doing wrong.
Tradition isn’t proof; follow guidance even when it’s new to you.
Every claim you make is recorded and will be asked about.
sections.hook: Ayat 22 and 23 are near twins: “we found our fathers upon a religion, and in their footsteps we are…” Only the last word changes: muhtadūn (22), muqtadūn (23).

sections.title: Ibrāhīm disowned idols; Makkah wanted a rich prophet, but gold means nothing
sections.meaning: Ibrāhīm, their ancestor, disowned his people’s idols and left tawḥīd as a lasting word among his descendants. Makkah enjoyed life until the truth came, then called it magic and wanted it sent to a great man. Allah divides provision and prophethood, and wealth is so small to Him that disbelievers could have silver houses.
points: Ibrāhīm: I disown what you worship, except my Creator
He left it a lasting word among his descendants
Makkah enjoyed life, then called the truth magic
“Why not a great man from the two cities?”
Do they divide Allah’s mercy? He divides even their livelihood
Silver ceilings, stairs, doors, couches and gold: only worldly enjoyment
sections.matters: It answers “our fathers” with their greatest father, Ibrāhīm, who broke from his. Then it tackles the objection that the Prophet ﷺ wasn’t rich, and gives the surah its name: gold is only enjoyment of this life.
sections.story: Quraysh asked why the Qur’an wasn’t sent to a great man of Makkah or Ṭāʾif. Names reported include al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah of Makkah and ʿUrwah ibn Masʿūd ath-Thaqafī of Ṭāʾif; other names are also reported.
explained: If they insist on following ancestors, why not Ibrāhīm, the noblest of them? He told his father and people, “I am free of what you worship, except the One who created me.” He made lā ilāha illā Allāh a word that lived on in his line, so they might return to it.

Instead, Makkah enjoyed long, easy lives, called the truth magic, and wanted a wealthy prophet. But Allah decides who receives His mercy. He even divides their livelihood, so people work for one another. Wealth is so small to Him that, if people wouldn’t all flock to disbelief, He’d give disbelievers houses of silver and gold.
teaches: Disown falsehood openly, not just privately.
Pass tawḥīd on to your children as a lasting word.
Allah, not people, chooses whom to honour.
Wealth is no sign that Allah loves someone.
sections.hook: The luxuries climb through a house: ceilings and stairways (33), doors and couches (34), then zukhruf, gold (35), the surah’s name. After “our fathers” (22–24), Ibrāhīm speaks to “his father” (26).

sections.title: Whoever ignores Allah’s reminder gets a devil companion; hold fast to revelation
sections.meaning: Whoever turns a blind eye to the Most Merciful’s reminder is given a devil as a constant companion. It blocks him from guidance while he thinks he is guided, until he meets Allah and wishes it were a world away. The Prophet ﷺ can’t make the deaf hear; he must hold fast to the Qur’an.
points: Ignore the reminder, get a devil companion who misleads you
On that Day: “I wish we were east and west apart!”
You can’t make the deaf hear or guide the blind
Whether you die first or see it, they will be punished
Hold fast to the revelation; it is an honour, and you’ll be asked
Ask earlier messengers: did We ever allow other gods?
sections.matters: It shows the cost of ignoring the reminder: a companion who makes falsehood look like guidance. It also reassures the Prophet ﷺ that results aren’t his burden, and that every messenger before him taught the same tawḥīd.
sections.story: No specific incident. The Prophet ﷺ is consoled while his enemies plot. Ayah 45 refers either to the messengers gathered for him on the Night Journey, or to asking the followers of earlier scriptures.
explained: Yaʿshu means to look with weak sight: to turn a blind eye to the Qur’an. Such a person is paired with a qarīn, a devil that stays with him, dressing up wrong as right. On the Day he comes to Allah, he wishes east and west lay between them. Sharing the punishment won’t ease it at all.

The Prophet ﷺ can’t make the deaf hear; his job is to convey. Whether Allah takes him first or shows him their punishment, it will come. So hold fast to the revelation: it is a straight path, an honour for him and his people, and they will be asked about it.
teaches: Neglecting the Qur’an invites company that makes wrong look right.
Feeling guided isn’t proof of being guided.
Convey the truth; guiding hearts belongs to Allah.
The Qur’an is an honour, and a responsibility you’ll be asked about.
sections.hook: Dhikr ar-Raḥmān opens it (36); dhikr and ar-Raḥmān return at 44 and 45. Qarīn, companion, appears twice: assigned in 36, cursed in 38 (biʾsa al-qarīn).

sections.title: Pharaoh’s people mock the signs; he scorns Mūsā, and all drown
sections.meaning: Mūsā came to Pharaoh with signs, and they laughed. Each sign was bigger than the last, and each punishment made them beg Mūsā to pray, then break their word. Pharaoh boasted of Egypt and its rivers, called Mūsā lowly and unclear, asked where his gold was, fooled his people, and they all drowned.
points: Mūsā brings the Lord’s signs; Pharaoh’s court laughs
Each sign greater than its sister; punishments to turn them back
“O magician, pray for us”; relief comes, they break their word
Pharaoh: Egypt and its rivers are mine; Mūsā is lowly
Why no gold bracelets, or angels at his side?
He fooled his people; they angered Allah and drowned, an example
sections.matters: Quraysh judged the Prophet ﷺ by wealth; Pharaoh judged Mūsā the same way. This section shows the objection is ancient, and how it ended: drowning, and a lesson for later generations.
sections.story: No specific incident. The story is told here because Quraysh’s objection, that the Prophet ﷺ wasn’t rich, was the same one Pharaoh raised against Mūsā.
explained: Mūsā came with signs like the staff and the shining hand, then punishments: flood, locusts, lice, frogs and blood, each greater than the last. Each time they called him “magician” (a title for a learned man in their eyes, or else mockery), promised to believe if he prayed, then broke their word.

Pharaoh gathered his people: isn’t Egypt mine, with the Nile’s channels flowing beneath my palaces? Am I not better than this weak man who can hardly speak clearly? Where are his gold bracelets, his escort of angels? He made fools of his people and they obeyed, so Allah drowned them all as a lesson.
teaches: Don’t judge the truth by the status of the one carrying it.
Promises made in hardship must be kept in ease.
Misleaders succeed with people already set on disobeying.
Those destroyed before us were made an example for us.
sections.hook: Two “idhā hum” reactions: they laughed (47), they broke their word (50). Gold links back: gold for disbelievers’ houses (35), gold bracelets Pharaoh demands for Mūsā (53).

sections.title: They cite ʿĪsā just to argue; he was only a favoured servant
sections.meaning: When ʿĪsā was brought up as an example, Quraysh cheered, thinking they had won the argument. It was only point-scoring. ʿĪsā was a servant Allah favoured and made a sign, and he is a sign of the Hour. He taught: Allah is my Lord and yours, so worship Him. Yet the factions split over him.
points: ʿĪsā raised as an example; they cheer: “Are our gods better, or he?”
Only a servant Allah favoured, an example for Banū Isrāʾīl
Allah could put angels on earth in your place
A sign of the Hour; follow Me; Shayṭān is your enemy
ʿĪsā: Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him
The factions differed; woe to the wrongdoers
sections.matters: It dismantles a debating trick and makes ʿĪsā’s true place clear: honoured, but a servant who called to Allah alone. It echoes ayah 45: no messenger, ʿĪsā included, ever taught worship of anyone but Allah.
sections.story: Reportedly, when “you and what you worship are fuel for Hell” (21:98) was revealed, ʿAbdullāh ibn az-Zibaʿrā asked: Christians worship ʿĪsā, so is he in Hell too? Quraysh cheered. Other reports say they claimed the Prophet ﷺ wanted to be worshipped like ʿĪsā.
explained: The ayah “you and what you worship are fuel for Hell” meant idols, and beings who wanted worship, not ʿĪsā, who never asked for it. Quraysh knew that and argued anyway. ʿĪsā was only a servant blessed with prophethood; his fatherless birth showed Allah’s power, the same power that could put angels on earth in your place.

He is a sign of the Hour: either his descent before it, or his birth proving resurrection. So don’t doubt it, and don’t let Shayṭān turn you away. ʿĪsā came with clear proofs, clarified their disputes and said: Allah is my Lord and yours, worship Him. Still, the factions split over him.
teaches: Arguing to win, not to find the truth, is a sign of going astray.
Honouring a prophet never means worshipping him.
Every prophet’s message is the same: worship Allah alone.
Shayṭān is a clear enemy; don’t let him turn you from the path.
sections.hook: Mathal chains the sections: Pharaoh’s people an example (56), ʿĪsā cited as an example (57) and made an example (59). “This is a straight path” closes both 61 and 64.

sections.title: Sudden Hour: friends become foes, believers enter Paradise, criminals stay in Hell
sections.meaning: The deniers are only waiting for the Hour to take them by surprise. Then friendships turn to hatred, except among the righteous. Believers hear “no fear, no grief” and enter Paradise, served from gold. Criminals stay in Hell with no relief, and Mālik tells them “you will remain.” Allah hears all their plots.
points: The Hour comes suddenly; friends become enemies, except the righteous
“O My servants, no fear”; enter Paradise with your spouses
Gold dishes, all souls desire, inherited for deeds, much fruit
Criminals in Hell forever, in despair; they wronged themselves
“O Mālik, let us die!” “You will remain”; you hated the truth
They plot, Allah plans; their secrets are heard and recorded
sections.matters: After all the arguments, this is where they lead: two destinations, forever. It also asks every friend what their friendship is built on, and tells the plotters of Makkah that Allah hears every secret.
sections.story: Ayah 67 was reportedly revealed about Umayyah ibn Khalaf and ʿUqbah ibn Abī Muʿayṭ, close friends who were both killed at Badr. Ayah 79 reportedly refers to Quraysh’s plot in Dār an-Nadwah to kill the Prophet ﷺ.
explained: The Hour will catch them off guard. Friendships built on anything but Allah turn into enmity; friends for Allah’s sake stay friends. A caller says “O My servants, no fear, no grief”, and everyone hopes, until “who believed in Our signs and were Muslims.” These enter Paradise delighted, served from gold, with all the soul desires, forever.

The criminals stay in Hell; it is never eased, and they fall silent in despair. Allah didn’t wrong them. They call to Mālik, the keeper of Hell, begging for death, and hear only “you will remain.” They hated the truth. If they plot, Allah plans too, and His angels write down their secrets.
teaches: Choose friends who will still be friends on the Day of Judgement.
Paradise is entered by Allah’s mercy; its ranks come by deeds.
In Hell there is no death and no relief.
No secret plan is hidden from Allah.
sections.hook: Two calls: Allah calls “O My servants” (68); the damned call “O Mālik” (77). Khālidūn, forever, ends 71 in Paradise and 74 in Hell.

sections.title: Allah has no son, He alone is God; turn away, saying “Peace”
sections.meaning: Say: if the Most Merciful had a son, I would be first to worship him, but He is far above that. He alone is God in heaven and on earth, and alone knows the Hour. False gods can’t intercede, and they admit Allah created them. The Prophet ﷺ is told: turn away and say “Peace.”
points: If Allah had a son, I’d worship first; He is far above it
Leave them to play until their promised Day
God in heaven and on earth; He alone knows the Hour
Their gods can’t intercede, only those who testify to the truth
Ask who created them: “Allah.” So how are they deceived?
“My Lord, they won’t believe.” Turn away, say “Peace”
sections.matters: It closes the case the surah opened: they admitted Allah is the Creator (9) and admit it again (87), so every other god collapses. And it ends with a model for calling people: argue with reason, then part with “Peace.”
sections.story: Ayah 86 reportedly came after an-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith and others of Quraysh said that if the Prophet ﷺ was right, they would take the angels as patrons, since the angels had more right to intercede for them.
explained: The Prophet ﷺ is the most devoted servant: if Allah truly had a son, he would be first to worship him. Since reason rules it out, he is first to deny it. Glory be to the Lord of the heavens, earth and Throne. He alone is God above and below, and He alone knows when the Hour comes.

The gods they call on can’t intercede; only those who testified to the truth knowingly can, by His leave. Ask who created them and they say Allah, so how do they turn away? Allah knows the Prophet’s ﷺ grief: “My Lord, these people won’t believe.” He is told: bear with them, say “Peace”, they will come to know.
teaches: Argue with reason, and be ready to accept what is truly proven.
Admitting Allah is the Creator means worshipping Him alone.
Intercession is only by Allah’s leave, for people of truth.
When talk turns ignorant, part with “Peace”, not insults.
sections.hook: Qul, “say”, opens it (81); “say, Peace” closes it (89). Ilāh comes twice in 84: in the heaven and on the earth. Ayah 87 repeats ayah 9’s question, “Who created…?”

groups.text: By the clear Book: Allah made it an Arabic Qur’an to be understood, high and wise with Him in the Mother of the Book.
Allah won’t stop sending the Reminder. Every prophet was mocked, and stronger nations were destroyed.
They admit Allah created the heavens and earth. He made the earth a bed and revives dead land with rain, as you will be raised.
He made the pairs, ships and cattle. When riding, thank Him and remember you will return to Him.
They make the angels Allah’s daughters, though a daughter’s birth darkens their own faces.
Did they witness the angels’ creation? Their claim is recorded. Blaming Allah’s will is only guessing.
They have no earlier book, only: “We found our fathers on a religion.”
The rich of every town said the same to every warner, rejected better guidance, and were punished.
Ibrāhīm disowned his people’s gods except his Creator, and left that word alive among his descendants.
Allah let Makkah enjoy life until the truth came; they called it magic.
They wanted a great man as prophet. Allah divides livelihood, and His mercy is better than their wealth.
Wealth is so small to Allah He’d give disbelievers silver houses and gold; the Hereafter is for the righteous.
Whoever ignores the reminder gets a devil companion who blocks the path while he thinks he is guided.
On the Day, he wishes his companion were a world away. Sharing the punishment helps no one.
You can’t make the deaf hear. Whether you die first or see it, they will be punished.
Hold fast to the revelation, an honour you’ll be asked about. No messenger ever taught other gods.
Mūsā came to Pharaoh with signs, each greater than the last. They laughed, so Allah seized them with punishments.
They begged “O magician, pray for us”, then broke their word as soon as relief came.
Pharaoh boasted of Egypt and its rivers and mocked Mūsā for having no gold or angels.
He fooled his people, they obeyed, and Allah drowned them all as a lesson for later peoples.
When ʿĪsā was cited as an example, Quraysh cheered and asked “Are our gods better, or he?”, just to argue.
ʿĪsā was only a favoured servant and a sign. Allah could even replace people with angels.
ʿĪsā is a sign of the Hour, so don’t doubt it; follow the straight path and don’t let Shayṭān block you.
ʿĪsā said: Allah is my Lord and yours, worship Him. Yet the factions split over him.
The Hour will come suddenly. Friends become enemies that Day, except those who feared Allah.
The believers are told: no fear, no grief. Enter Paradise with your spouses, delighted.
Gold dishes and whatever souls desire, forever: a Paradise inherited for deeds, full of fruit.
The criminals stay in Hell with no relief, in despair. Allah didn’t wrong them.
They beg Mālik for death and are told they will remain. They hated the truth.
If they plot, Allah plans. He hears their secrets, and His angels record them.
If the Most Merciful had a son, I would be first to worship; He is far above that. Leave them.
He alone is God in heaven and on earth, owns everything, and alone knows the Hour.
Their gods can’t intercede. They admit Allah created them, so how are they turned away?
The Prophet ﷺ complains of their disbelief. He is told: turn aside, say “Peace”; they will come to know.

1.explain: Ḥā Mīm: separate letters whose meaning Allah alone knows. They were not sent down without purpose.

2.explain: An oath by the Qur’an itself, al-kitāb al-mubīn: clear, and making clear what people need for this life, their religion and the next.

3.explain: It was made an Arabic Qur’an, in the clearest language, so that you, starting with the people of Makkah, would understand its words and meanings.

4.explain: Umm al-kitāb is the Preserved Tablet. With Allah the Qur’an is ʿaliyy, high in honour, and ḥakīm, full of wisdom, so people on earth should honour it too.

5.explain: Should We stop sending you the Reminder just because you go too far? Either: no, in His mercy He kept sending it; or: do you think you’ll be left unpunished?

6.explain: Allah sent many prophets to the earlier peoples. He never leaves people without guidance.

7.explain: Every one of them was mocked. This consoles the Prophet ﷺ: his people’s mockery is nothing new.

8.explain: Nations far mightier than Quraysh were destroyed. Mathal al-awwalīn: their story and the lesson of their punishment have already been told.

9.explain: Ask them who created the heavens and earth and they say: the Mighty, the Knowing. They admit He is the only Creator, yet worship others alongside Him.

10.explain: Mahd: a bed, like a child’s cradle, stable enough to live on. The roads through mountains and valleys guide your journeys, and guide you to reflect.

11.explain: Rain comes bi-qadar, in the amount needed, not as a destroying flood. It revives dead land, and that is how you will be brought out of your graves.

12.explain: Al-azwāj: all the pairs and kinds of things. He gave you ships and animals to ride, both of them His blessings.

13.explain: Settled on its back, remember His favour and say: subḥāna alladhī sakhkhara lanā hādhā. The Prophet ﷺ said it when mounting. Muqrinīn: we could never have mastered it ourselves.

14.explain: “And to our Lord we will return.” Every earthly journey is a reminder of the last journey, to the Hereafter, and of the provision it needs.

15.explain: Juzʾ: a part. Calling angels Allah’s daughters makes some of His servants part of Him, since a child is part of its parent. Kafūr mubīn: man is plainly ungrateful.

16.explain: A sharp rebuke: would He take daughters from what He creates and choose sons for you? That would make them better off than their Lord.

17.explain: When one of them is told a daughter was born to him, his face darkens and he is kaẓīm, choked with grief. Yet this is what he attributes to the Most Merciful.

18.explain: In their view, a daughter is raised in ḥilyah, ornaments, and can’t make her case clearly in a dispute. So how can they give Allah what they count as lesser?

19.explain: They called the angels, who are servants of the Most Merciful, female. Did they witness their creation? Their testimony will be recorded, and they will be questioned about it.
19.why: Reportedly, the Prophet ﷺ asked them how they knew the angels were female. They said they heard it from their fathers and testified that their fathers did not lie. This ayah answered them.

20.explain: They claim Allah’s will proves He approves of their worship (of the angels, or the idols). Yakhruṣūn: they are only guessing. His will covers all that happens; His approval is known from His books.

21.explain: Or did We give them a book before the Qur’an, telling them to worship others, that they hold on to? No, that never happened.

22.explain: Their only argument: “We found our fathers on an ummah”, a religion and way, “and we are guided by following in their footsteps.”
22.why: Reportedly revealed about Quraysh leaders: al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah, Abū Sufyān, Abū Jahl, and ʿUtbah and Shaybah, the sons of Rabīʿah.

23.explain: Nothing new: in every town the mutrafūn, those spoiled by wealth and power, gave every warner the same answer. Muqtadūn: we follow their lead.

24.explain: The warner asked: even if I bring you better guidance than your fathers had? They said: we reject whatever you were sent with. They wanted their ways, not guidance.

25.explain: So Allah took revenge on those nations. See how the deniers ended, and let Quraysh beware of the same.

26.explain: Ibrāhīm, the ancestor Quraysh were proud of, told his father and people: innanī barāʾ, I am completely free of what you worship. He rejected his fathers’ religion out loud.

27.explain: Except the One who faṭaranī, created me. He will guide me: as He set my body and life right, He will set right my religion and my Hereafter.

28.explain: Kalimah bāqiyah: the word of tawḥīd, lā ilāha illā Allāh, kept alive among his descendants, so that they, the people of Makkah included, might return to it.

29.explain: Yet Allah let these people and their fathers enjoy life, without rushing their punishment, until the truth, the Qur’an, came with a Messenger who made everything clear.

30.explain: When the truth came, they called it magic and rejected it. Their easy lives had made them arrogant.

31.explain: Why wasn’t this Qur’an sent to a great man of the two cities, Makkah and Ṭāʾif? They reportedly meant men like al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah or ʿUrwah ibn Masʿūd ath-Thaqafī.

32.explain: Are they in charge of Allah’s mercy, prophethood? He divides even their livelihood and ranks, sukhriyyan, so some employ others. His mercy is better than all the wealth they gather.

33.explain: If all people weren’t going to rush into disbelief for wealth, Allah would give disbelievers ceilings of silver and silver stairways, maʿārij, to climb to their roofs.

34.explain: …and silver doors for their houses, and silver couches to recline on.

35.explain: …and zukhruf, gold. All of it is brief worldly enjoyment; the Hereafter is for the muttaqīn. The Prophet ﷺ said: if this world weighed a gnat’s wing to Allah, no disbeliever would get a sip of water.

36.explain: Yaʿshu: turns a blind eye to the dhikr of the Most Merciful, the Qur’an. Allah assigns him a devil as qarīn, a companion that stays with him and makes falsehood look good.

37.explain: These devils block them from the path, yet they are sure they are guided. There is no excuse: they turned from the reminder when guidance was within reach.

38.explain: When he comes to Us (another reading: when both come to Us), he tells his companion: I wish we were as far apart as east and west. What an evil companion!

39.explain: It will be said: sharing the punishment won’t help you. In this world shared hardship feels lighter; there it lightens nothing. Or: your regret won’t help you today.

40.explain: Can you make the deaf hear or guide the blind? Guidance isn’t in your hands, only conveying the message. They chose deafness and blindness by turning away.

41.explain: If We take you away in death before punishing them, We will still take revenge on them.

42.explain: Or We will show you, in your lifetime, the punishment promised them; We have full power over them. This is usually taken to mean what they met at Badr.

43.explain: So hold fast to what is revealed to you, in belief and in practice. You are on a straight path, built on truth while others build on doubt.

44.explain: Dhikr here means an honour for you and your people, since it came in their language, and also a reminder. You will all be asked how you lived by it.

45.explain: Ask the messengers sent before you: did We ever make other gods to be worshipped? Either literally, on the Night Journey, or by asking their scriptures and followers. The answer: all taught tawḥīd.

46.explain: Allah sent Mūsā with His signs to Pharaoh and his chiefs. His message: I am the messenger of the Lord of the worlds, so worship Him alone.

47.explain: When he showed them the signs, they laughed at them. The signs were clear; they mocked out of arrogance.

48.explain: Each sign was greater than its ukht, its sister before it. Allah also seized them with punishments (flood, locusts, lice, frogs and blood) so they might return to faith.

49.explain: Yā ayyuha as-sāḥir: either mockery, or respect, since magicians were their scholars. Pray to your Lord by the promise He made you, and we will surely be guided.

50.explain: When Allah lifted the punishment through Mūsā’s prayer, they broke their promise at once and held on to disbelief.

51.explain: Pharaoh proclaimed: isn’t the kingdom of Egypt mine, and these rivers, the Nile’s channels, flowing beneath my palaces? Don’t you see my greatness? He boasted of things outside himself.

52.explain: Am I not better than this mahīn, weak and insignificant, who can hardly speak clearly? Mūsā’s tongue was burned by a coal as a child; Allah had eased it at his request. Pharaoh was misleading.

53.explain: Their custom was to put gold bracelets on a man they made chief. Why hasn’t Mūsā got those, or angels at his side to vouch for him? He judged only by appearances.

54.explain: Fa-stakhaffa qawmahu: he made fools of his people, or easily swayed them, and they obeyed. They were already fāsiqīn, defiantly disobedient, which is why his tricks worked.

55.explain: Āsafūnā: they angered Us, meaning their deeds made them deserve punishment. So Allah took revenge and drowned them all.

56.explain: Salaf: a precedent, going ahead of all who do the same. Mathal: a lesson for later peoples to learn from.

57.explain: When ʿĪsā son of Maryam was cited as an example, your people yaṣiddūn: raised an uproar of delight (or, in another reading, turned away), sure they had won the argument.
57.why: Reportedly, after 21:98 (“you and what you worship are fuel for Hell”), Ibn az-Zibaʿrā argued that Christians worship ʿĪsā and Jews ʿUzayr: are they in Hell? Quraysh cheered. Other reports say they claimed the Prophet ﷺ wanted to be worshipped like ʿĪsā.

58.explain: “Are our gods better, or is he?” (He: ʿĪsā, or in one view the Prophet ﷺ.) They raised it only for jadal, argument, knowing the ayah meant idols. They are a quarrelsome people.

59.explain: ʿĪsā was only a servant whom Allah favoured with prophethood. His birth without a father made him a sign for Banū Isrāʾīl of Allah’s power to do whatever He wills.

60.explain: If Allah willed, He could replace you with angels living on earth, succeeding one another. Creating the unusual is easy for Him, and it makes no one divine.

61.explain: La-ʿilmun lis-sāʿah: ʿĪsā is a sign of the Hour, either by his descent before it or by his fatherless birth proving resurrection. So don’t doubt it; follow Me, this is the straight path.

62.explain: Don’t let Shayṭān turn you away from following the truth. He is your open enemy, eager to mislead you.

63.explain: ʿĪsā came with clear proofs and al-ḥikmah, prophethood, to clarify some of what they disputed in religion. So fear Allah and obey me.

64.explain: “Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him.” ʿĪsā called himself a servant like them, not a son or partner of God. That is the straight path.

65.explain: The aḥzāb, factions, split over him: some said he was Allah’s servant and messenger, which is true; others called him God’s son, or God. Woe to the wrongdoers on a painful Day.

66.explain: What are they waiting for, except the Hour arriving suddenly while they don’t notice? When it comes, regret won’t help them.

67.explain: Al-akhillāʾ, close friends, become enemies that Day, cursing each other, except the muttaqīn: friends for Allah’s sake stay friends in both worlds.
67.why: Reportedly revealed about Umayyah ibn Khalaf and ʿUqbah ibn Abī Muʿayṭ, close friends. When ʿUqbah sat with the Prophet ﷺ, Umayyah pressed him to spit at him, and he did. Both were killed at Badr.

68.explain: Yā ʿibādī: no fear about what lies ahead, no grief over what is past. Reportedly everyone hopes on hearing this call, until the next ayah says whom it is for.

69.explain: Those who believed in Our signs, understanding and acting on them, and were Muslims, submitting inside and out. At this, all but the believers lose hope.

70.explain: Enter Paradise, you and your azwāj: your spouses, or those like you in faith. Tuḥbarūn: delighted and honoured beyond words.

71.explain: Plates of gold and cups without handles are passed around them. There is whatever souls desire and eyes delight in, and they stay there forever.

72.explain: This is the Paradise you inherited for what you did. Entry is by Allah’s mercy; deeds are its cause, and they decide your rank.

73.explain: Plenty of fruit of every kind to eat, whatever you choose. Whatever is picked is replaced.

74.explain: Al-mujrimūn, the criminals who disbelieved, stay in the punishment of Hell forever, surrounded by it on every side.

75.explain: It is never eased, not even for a moment. Mublisūn: in despair of any good, fallen silent.

76.explain: Allah did not wrong them. They wronged themselves by rejecting the truth after it was made clear.

77.explain: They call Mālik, the keeper of Hell: let your Lord finish us off! He answers, reportedly after a long wait (forty or a thousand years): mākithūn, you are staying.

78.explain: We brought you the truth, made clear, but most of you hated it. That is why you are here.

79.explain: Abramū amran: have they settled on a plot against the Prophet ﷺ? Then Allah is settling a plan too, one that overturns theirs.
79.why: Reportedly revealed about Quraysh’s meeting in Dār an-Nadwah, where they agreed that a man from every clan would join in killing the Prophet ﷺ, so no one could avenge him. The plotters were killed at Badr.

80.explain: Do they think Allah doesn’t hear their sirr, what is in their hearts, and their najwā, whispered talk? Yes He does, and His angels with them write it all down.

81.explain: Say: if the Most Merciful had a son, I would be first to worship him. That isn’t possible; the point is that the Prophet ﷺ rejects it on reason, not stubbornness.

82.explain: Subḥān: exalted is the Lord of the heavens, the earth and the Throne above what they describe: a son, a partner or a helper.

83.explain: Leave them to yakhūḍū, plunge into falsehood, and play in their worldly lives, until they meet their promised Day, the Day of Resurrection.

84.explain: He alone is ilāh, the One truly worshipped, in the heaven and on the earth. He is al-Ḥakīm, wise in all He does, and al-ʿAlīm, knowing everything.

85.explain: Tabāraka: blessed and exalted is the Owner of the heavens, earth and all between. Only He knows when the Hour will come, and to Him you will all return.

86.explain: The gods they call on can’t intercede. The exception: those who knowingly testified lā ilāha illā Allāh, such as ʿĪsā, ʿUzayr and the angels, who intercede for believers by His leave.
86.why: Reportedly, an-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith and others of Quraysh said: if what Muhammad ﷺ says is true, we take the angels as our patrons; they have more right to intercede for us than he does.

87.explain: Ask them who created them and they say “Allah.” Fa-annā yuʾfakūn: then how are they turned away? Admitting He is the Creator obliges worshipping Him alone.

88.explain: Wa qīlihi: the Prophet’s ﷺ saying, complaining to his Lord: “My Lord, these are a people who will not believe.” Allah knows it, and is patient with them so they might repent.

89.explain: Fa-ṣfaḥ: turn aside and bear their harm. Say “Salām”: a word of parting, not a greeting. This came before fighting was ordered. They will come to know the result.
